transcript.speaker: DOCTOR

transcript.speaker: PATIENT

transcript.speaker: DOCTOR
transcript.text: OK. So not like taking a deep breath or anything like that?

transcript.text: Maybe taking a deep breath.

transcript.speaker: DOCTOR
transcript.text: OK. And when the pain started, could you tell me, could you think of anything that you were doing at the time?

transcript.text: OK. So you didn't feel like you hurt yourself when you were doing that? No. OK. And in regards to how severe the pain is on a scale of one to ten, ten being the worst pain you've ever felt, how severe would you say the pain is?

transcript.speaker: PATIENT
transcript.text: Hey Doc, I'm a 45 year old man coming in. I'm worried there's a little rash on my leg. I'm getting nervous about.

transcript.speaker: DOCTOR
transcript.text: Well, hi. So you, I understand you have a rash on your leg.

transcript.speaker: PATIENT
transcript.text: I don't really know what I would call it. That's what I told the nurse when I came in, but it's more hurts than anything.

transcript.speaker: DOCTOR
transcript.text: Okay. How long has this been going on for?

transcript.speaker: PATIENT
transcript.text: It's been, it's been looking weird for about a week, but only yes, it started hurting yesterday. It's sort of looking strange. And I just wanted to come in and get it checked out.

transcript.speaker: DOCTOR
transcript.text: Okay. When you say it's looking strange, can you tell me what you mean by that?

transcript.speaker: PATIENT
transcript.text: Swollen. It looks bigger than it did before. And meaner, if that makes sense.

transcript.speaker: DOCTOR
transcript.text: Swollen. Okay. Is it red?

transcript.speaker: PATIENT
transcript.text: Yeah, it's red. It's turning more red, kind of in the area around it. I've got these, I got these scabs. I've got diabetes and not exactly the best with it. I'm scratching at it. And normally it's not that bad, but this is just strange looking. There's no other word for it.

transcript.speaker: DOCTOR
transcript.text: Okay. Have you ever had anything like this before? I guess you kind of just said that you didn't, but I'll double check.

transcript.speaker: PATIENT
transcript.text: No, no. Well, I've had, I have occasional ulcers and sometimes I've banged my toe and I'm not exactly the best taking care of my feet, but this is the first time I've gone something that, I don't know, I've just never seen it before.

transcript.speaker: DOCTOR
transcript.text: Okay. Do you have any ulcers right now, let me see.

transcript.speaker: PATIENT
transcript.text: I think so. I don't want to last time I saw the family dog. I think I've got an ulcer on my left heel, but I think it's doing all right.

transcript.speaker: DOCTOR
transcript.text: Okay. And what leg are you having this problem with right now?

transcript.speaker: PATIENT
transcript.text: So am I right? So my ankle.

transcript.speaker: DOCTOR
transcript.text: Okay. How have your sugars been controlled recently?

transcript.speaker: PATIENT
transcript.text: I stopped measuring them. Yeah. Last time I measured it was pretty bad. I think I A1C last time was like nine, nine something. I'm trying better to be with it. This is hard with work, you know?

transcript.speaker: DOCTOR
transcript.text: For sure, I can imagine. So in general, even if you don't know your numbers for your sugars, have you felt worse than usual lately? Have you felt run down at all?

transcript.speaker: PATIENT
transcript.text: Yeah, actually I have pain more, feel hungry, sometimes it's tired, but I don't know. It's hard to tell there's an awful lot going on in my life right now with the kids, but it's hard to tell. I think yeah, I need to see my family dog.

transcript.speaker: DOCTOR
transcript.text: Okay. Definitely, you know, a good idea moving forward just to make sure you get on top of these things, but I'm glad you came in today so we can, you know, have a better look at you and make sure that there's nothing super concerning going on. transcript.speaker: PATIENT
transcript.text: Symptoms, I feel a little hot actually when the swelling started, it also started leaking. That's like white stuff from one of the, one of what used to be a scab. So now like kind of open the wound now.

transcript.speaker: DOCTOR
transcript.text: Okay. Okay, so when did you start feeling hot?

transcript.speaker: PATIENT
transcript.text: Honestly, last 12 hours.

transcript.speaker: DOCTOR
transcript.text: Okay. Can you take your temperature at all?

transcript.speaker: PATIENT
transcript.text: No, I don't have a thermometer at home.

transcript.speaker: DOCTOR
transcript.text: Have you had any difficulty breathing?

transcript.speaker: PATIENT
transcript.text: No, no.

transcript.speaker: DOCTOR
transcript.text: Any chest pain? No. Have you noticed that your left, sorry, your right leg feels any hotter than the left?

transcript.speaker: PATIENT
transcript.text: Yeah, yeah, it does actually. Changing socks the other day. Yeah.

transcript.speaker: DOCTOR
transcript.text: Hey, have you, have you felt ill recently? Have you been sick at all?

transcript.speaker: PATIENT
transcript.text: Mm. Satch, I'm just feeling overall crummy last couple of weeks. No, don't really, less energy today, but I was up last night thinking about this. Yeah. I wanted to come in and talk.

transcript.speaker: DOCTOR
transcript.text: Okay. Yeah, I'm, if you do did the right thing, I'm glad that you're in today. Is the pain on your legs worst when you catch it?

transcript.speaker: DOCTOR
transcript.text: Okay. Okay.

transcript.speaker: PATIENT
transcript.text: Just resting it right now, it feels fine.

transcript.text: It's okay. Okay. transcript.text: Chronic condition. I see the family talk about cholesterol. I want to pill for that. Had asthma as a kid. Not too much of an issue now. And my back, I've had back pain for the last 10 years, but I don't really really take for his tile and all that bill for that. Okay. Okay.

transcript.text: That makes sense. Okay. So, sorry, I put a side track to there. So we talked about re -diabetes. You said you have high cholesterol. So what medications are you currently taking?

transcript.speaker: PATIENT

transcript.speaker: PATIENT
transcript.text: No. Okay.

transcript.speaker: DOCTOR
transcript.text: Are you on any medication new to your resume?

transcript.speaker: PATIENT
transcript.text: No, no, but I had them for about a year now.

transcript.speaker: DOCTOR
transcript.text: Do you have any allergies?

transcript.speaker: PATIENT

transcript.speaker: DOCTOR
transcript.text: Okay. Is that the only surgery that you've had? Yeah. Um, and can you tell me, do you have any family history of diabetes, skin problems, anything else that stands out to you?

transcript.speaker: PATIENT
transcript.text: Yep. On the side of the family, pretty much everyone has diabetes, high blood pressure, cholesterol. That side of the family is pretty healthy. Um, I think maybe one of my aunts had lung cancer, but she's a pretty big smoker too.

transcript.speaker: DOCTOR
transcript.text: Um, and I'm just gonna ask you a few questions about your lifestyle. So you said that you have children?

transcript.speaker: PATIENT
transcript.text: Yeah, I do.

transcript.speaker: DOCTOR
transcript.text: You live in town. Do you live with your kids?

transcript.speaker: PATIENT
transcript.text: Uh, I live in town. I see my kids every two weeks.

transcript.speaker: DOCTOR
transcript.text: And what do you do for work? Did I already ask you this?

transcript.speaker: PATIENT
transcript.text: Uh, no, I'm currently unemployed. I'm looking for work partially employed. I suppose you should say it for my own business.

transcript.speaker: DOCTOR
transcript.text: I see. And what do you, uh, what do you do when, uh, when you are working, ideally?

transcript.speaker: PATIENT
transcript.text: Uh, I am working. I'm an accountant.

transcript.speaker: DOCTOR
transcript.text: Okay, cool. Um, and do you smoke?

transcript.speaker: PATIENT
transcript.text: Um, yeah, once in a while. Yeah. I'm stressed though. I've got some

transcript.speaker: DOCTOR
transcript.text: smoke on average.

transcript.speaker: PATIENT
transcript.text: Last couple of weeks I've been smoking more. Maybe like two packs a week.

transcript.speaker: DOCTOR
transcript.text: Okay. Do you drink alcohol? Yeah. How much do you typically drink? Uh,

transcript.speaker: PATIENT
transcript.text: average week, maybe a two, four.

transcript.speaker: DOCTOR
transcript.text: So maybe like three per day or something like that. If you were to average it out.

transcript.speaker: PATIENT
transcript.text: Yeah, if you average it out, I mainly go through the two, four on a weekend, to be honest.

transcript.speaker: DOCTOR
transcript.text: Oh, I see. Okay. More so on the weekend. So maybe a little bit more than three per day. That's on those days. Okay. Oh, I see this. That does everything. That's, I need to ask you for now. I'd like to get a closer look at this leg. Um, did you have any other questions or concerns before we move forward to physical exam?

transcript.speaker: PATIENT
transcript.text: No, I just want to get this figured out.

transcript.speaker: DOCTOR
transcript.text: Okay. Yeah, we'll definitely do that for you. Uh, so yeah, I'm going to have a look at it and then after that I will go talk to the doctor that I'm working with and we'll see what we can do for you. Does that sound good?

transcript.speaker: PATIENT
transcript.text: Thank you, Doc. Yeah, sounds great.

transcript.speaker: DOCTOR
transcript.text: Awesome. Okay. Thanks.
